section_summary: This section contains two press clippings on Japan’s wartime shortages, a Peiping embassy despatch transmitting M. S. Bates’s observations, two cross-reference notes, and part of a report on economic conditions in September 1939. The documents describe shortages of labor, fuel and consumer goods, rising prices, political attitudes toward the war in China, and Japan’s response to the outbreak of war in Europe.

people.name: M. S. Bates
people.role: University of Nanking scholar and author of “Notes from Japan”

people.name: Gourley
people.role: Sender of a Kobe report cited in a cross-reference note

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: Sender of a Japan report cited in a cross-reference note

subfiles.title: Unidentified article on Japan’s wartime shortages
subfiles.about: Labor conscription, rationing, inflation and material shortages in wartime Japan.
subfiles.summary: The article describes labor and supply shortages and argues that mounting unrest may affect army policy.

subfiles.title: Timeless Shivers in Japan
subfiles.from: Staff correspondent, The Christian Science Monitor
subfiles.about: Fuel and electricity shortages in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The correspondent reports power cuts, coal and charcoal rationing, gasoline shortages and rising prices.

subfiles.title: Transmission of “Notes from Japan”
subfiles.from: Frank P. Lockhart, for the Ambassador, Peiping
subfiles.about: Forwards M. S. Bates’s report and the Nanking covering despatch.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart says recent travelers’ accounts generally support Bates’s observations on commodity prices and labor conditions.

subfiles.title: Covering despatch for “Notes from Japan”
subfiles.from: J. Hall Paxton, for the Consul General at Shanghai
subfiles.about: Forwards Bates’s report and comments on his reliability.
subfiles.summary: Paxton describes the report as a careful study of recent economic and political conditions in Japan.

subfiles.title: Notes from Japan
subfiles.about: Observations on Japan’s economy, politics and war policy based on an August–September visit.
subfiles.summary: Bates finds shortages and rising prices but concludes that Japan can sustain its current economic effort for some time. He describes broad public support for the war alongside declining enthusiasm, views of Wang Jingwei, fighting on the Mongolian frontier, cabinet changes and possible strategies for ending the war in China.

subfiles.title: Japanese Youth Volunteer Summer Workers on the Continent of Asia
subfiles.about: Points to a detailed report on Japanese youth volunteer summer workers in Asia.
subfiles.summary: References an October 18 Kobe report filed as 894.00/881.

subfiles.title: General Economic Conditions in Japan During September 1939
subfiles.about: Points to a report on Japan’s economic conditions in September 1939.
subfiles.summary: References Grew’s October 16 report, filed as 894.00 P.R./142.

subfiles.title: General Economic and Financial Conditions
subfiles.from: Grew, with assistance from the Office of the Commercial Attaché
subfiles.about: Japan’s economic and financial position after war began in Europe.
subfiles.summary: The report describes a brief stock market surge, government controls and Japan’s hopes of expanding exports and shipping. It weighs those opportunities against scarce raw materials, import restrictions, higher costs and limited shipping capacity. It also records new export and fuel controls, September price rises and the yen’s shift from sterling to a dollar peg.
